questions.prompt: What do slots let a parent pass into a child that props cannot?
questions.explanation: Props pass data values; slots pass template markup, letting the parent supply content that the child renders in a <slot> outlet.

questions.prompt: What is the content written between <slot>…</slot> tags?

options.text: Fallback content, shown only when the parent provides nothing for that slot

questions.explanation: Content inside a <slot> is fallback content; it renders only if the parent doesn't fill that slot.

questions.prompt: How does a parent fill a named slot called "footer"?
questions.explanation: The parent uses <template #footer> (shorthand for v-slot:footer), which fills the child's <slot name="footer">.

questions.prompt: Why can't ordinary slot content read the child's internal variables?

options.text: Because slot content is compiled in the parent's scope, not the child's
Because variables are private in JavaScript

questions.explanation: Slot content lives in the parent's scope. To expose child data, use a scoped slot: the child binds data on <slot :item="x" /> and the parent receives it.

questions.prompt: A slot that passes data from the child to the slot content is called a ______ slot. (one word)
questions.explanation: Scoped slots expose slot props from the child, so the parent can render child-owned data (like each item in a list).

questions.prompt: You want a reusable list component that iterates items internally but lets the parent decide how each row looks. What do you use?

options.text: A scoped slot exposing each item

questions.explanation: A scoped slot lets the child own iteration while exposing each item to the parent, which supplies the row markup — the ideal pattern for flexible list/renderer components.
